To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) leaching fraction was found highly dependent on transpiration and 2) transpiration was highly dependent on root zone salinization.

(1) The leaching fraction is not constant but is affected by root zone salinity and the plant feedback mechanism; (2) Increasing the amount of irrigation water application increases the transpiration and yields of the bell pepper crop, and (3) The higher the irrigation water salinity level, and the higher the leaching fraction, the greater the yield benefit from increased leachate volume.

The effect of salinity of irrigation waters on crop transpiration, leaching requirements, and yields was studied for bell pepper in the Arava valley of Israel, and it was found that leaching fraction was highly influenced by plant transpiration, as it was affected by root zone salinity, while increased irrigation with saline water led to increased yields.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between the salinity of water and the amount of applied water.
water quantity-saline interactions, which are of major importance to the management of irrigated agriculture in arid regions.
the effect of the salinity of the irrigation water on the leaching requirement for maximizing crop yields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of the amount applied irrigation water on transpiration and leaching fractions depends on the salinity of the irrigation water.
the effect of irrigation water salinities on transpiration and yields depends on the amount of water applied, on the salinity levels and on the crop.
, for a given soil, crop and climate, the amount of water required for irrigation is a function of the salinity of the irrigation water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, when irrigating with high-saline water, leaching is needed to prevent salt accumulation in the root zone.
the use of saline irrigation water for crops grown in protected environments is possible but that the amount of water needed for leaching is high.

, for the bell pepper case study crop, the leaching fraction needed to achieve maximum yield when irrigating with water salinity levels of 2.5, 5.0, and 10.0 dS m-1 was 0.4, 0.5, and 0.7, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when irrigating with water of high salinity, it is important to apply enough irrigation water to satisfy plant transpiration needs.

when irrigation water salinity is high, the leaching requirement is very large, and it is therefore highly important to minimize the amount of irrigation applied, and to maximize the use of water of high quality.
, when irrigation with saline water, leaching fraction should be kept at a minimum, to avoid excessive water use.
